_doc: What this adapter can actually enforce, in the four words core uses:
enforced, prefix-allowlist, prompt-only, pending. A profile that
*requires* a capability missing from the map below is refused rather
than run under a restriction that exists only in the prompt — see
setup: Needs the opencode CLI on this machine's PATH (or BOARD_OPENCODE_BIN naming it), with a provider configured. Model names are opencode's own "provider/model-id". Its event bridge is a plugin wired into the application by install.py; an external layout cannot wire it.

_doc: How this adapter may be inspected without a vendor binary — the
contract is in core/adapters/README.md. `describe` is the command
that prints what this adapter would hand opencode for one launch,
run with this directory as its working directory; `stubEnv` names
the variable that replaces the binary so `run` can be exercised.

unsupported.filesystem-sandbox: opencode's permission rules are globs over tool inputs and command lines; they cannot confine a run's reads to a named set of files.
unsupported.network-policy: opencode exposes no network boundary this adapter could set
